context.in_practice: On route 1, `.0` under a key that doesn't exist yet creates a one-item list, and that works at any depth. Any other index under a missing key fails. On route 2, a digit-only segment can never create anything, so a new list can't be started with `config set`. Both routes append when the index equals the current length.
context.stakes: Whether a user can start a brand-new list by setting index 0 under a key that doesn't exist yet. On route 1 that works. On route 2 it is refused, and the user has to create the list some other way first. Both routes append to an existing list when the index equals its length.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 lets a user start a list with `config set`, but `.0` quietly gets the extra meaning "create a list". Route 2 keeps path creation to plain keys only, but a user cannot start a new list from the command line.

plan_why: Sets a list index under a missing key: 0 (route 1 creates a new list, route 2 exits 5), a nonzero index (both should exit 5), a nested missing parent ending in 0, and index == length on an existing list (both append). A final show prints the resulting config.
routes: A `0` segment under a missing parent creates a new list; any other index exits 5
Missing segments are created only as mapping keys; a missing digit segment exits 5; index == length appends, larger indexes exit 5
